newsitem.title: GERMANY: Reward to help find kidnapped German businessman.
newsitem.headline: Reward to help find kidnapped German businessman.

text.p: The family of a kidnapped multi-millionaire Frankfurt businessman offered a one million mark ($650,000) reward on Monday for help in finding him, German police said.

Jakub Fiszmann, 40, was violently abducted at the beginning of this month. Even though his brother Georg met the kidnappers' demands and paid a four million mark ransom last week, the kidnappers did not release Fiszmann as promised.
"The family of the kidnap victim have offered a reward of one million marks for information that contributes to finding the victim or his location," a police spokeswoman said in a statement.
Police scoured the countryside north of Frankfurt on Monday for clues to Fiszmann's whereabouts. They said at the weekend they believed he was still alive and held near the city.
The Fiszmann family is one of the wealthiest in Germany. Police confirmed reports at the weekend that the family had total assets exceeding 400 million marks.
Hundreds of German police searched an area of forest and fields near the town of Idstein north of Frankfurt.
Searchers used helicopters and tracker dogs to comb the area after an anonymous phone call said cars had been seen in the area, and police said they might have been involved.
They were also looking for dug-outs in the earth which could be used to hide Fiszmann.
The last definite sign of life from Fiszmann came on October 2, one day after he was kidnapped, during which he was injured in a scuffle.
Fiszmann telephoned a contact, believed to be his girlfriend, saying he was being held by kidnappers in a cellar.
A ransom of 3.5 million marks was set, later raised to four million marks.
Fiszmann needs medication to treat specific food allergies so police are watching out for sales of certain drugs.
The police also released further information about the white Fiat Ducato van used during the kidnapping.
